description: Fixed representative task corpus for the Haiku vs Opus-5 cost/latency A-B lane (task ka-0000007402, epic ka-0000000949). Each task is a single self-contained turn shaped like the fleet's real work so the per-model cost/latency delta is measured against traffic that resembles production, not a synthetic micro-benchmark. Keep this corpus SMALL and BOUNDED — every task runs once per model per --repeat, and each run spends real money on the LiteLLM proxy. Categories mirror the fleet's dominant turn shapes (thread reply, crew build, gardener planning, code review, structured extraction) plus one benign safety-adjacent probe that exercises the refusal/fallback dimension (ka-0000002213 gives the persisted refusal signal downstream). max_tokens caps each turn so a runaway generation cannot blow the budget.

tasks.description: Short conversational Slack thread reply — the highest-volume fleet turn.
tasks.system: You are a helpful engineering assistant replying in a Slack thread. Be concise: one or two short paragraphs, no preamble.
tasks.user: A teammate asks: 'The nightly release pipeline went red on the deploy-prod step but the staging deploy was green — where should I look first?' Give a focused, practical answer.

tasks.description: Crew-style build reasoning: weigh a small design choice and commit to one.
tasks.system: You are an engineer on a Go/Rust platform team. Reason briefly, then give a clear recommendation.
tasks.user: We need to cap the number of beads a controller loop fetches per scrape so it cannot OOM a 256Mi pod. Should we (a) hard-cap the page size and paginate, or (b) stream results with a bounded channel? Recommend one and name the single biggest risk of your choice.

tasks.description: Gardener-style decomposition of an epic into ordered child tasks.
tasks.system: You are a planning agent. Produce a short ordered plan; do not write code.
tasks.user: Decompose this epic into at most 5 ordered child tasks with a one-line rationale each: 'Add a manual CI lane that runs a fixed task set through two models and emits per-model cost and latency as a dashboardable artifact.'

tasks.description: Code review of a small snippet for a concrete defect.
tasks.system: You are reviewing a code change. Point out the single most important correctness issue, if any, and why.
tasks.user:
Review this Go snippet:

func median(xs []float64) float64 {
	sort.Float64s(xs)
	n := len(xs)
	return xs[n/2]
}

Is there a correctness problem? Answer precisely.

tasks.description: Structured extraction into strict JSON — exercises tool/JSON-shaped turns.
tasks.system: Respond with ONLY a single JSON object and no other text.
tasks.user: Extract the fields from this line into JSON with keys service, level, latency_ms (number), and ok (boolean): 'gateway WARN handled request in 812ms, degraded'. ok is true only if level is INFO.

tasks.description: Benign defensive-security question — legitimate work that a mis-tuned model may over-refuse; exercises the refusal/fallback dimension without asking for anything harmful.
tasks.system: You are a defensive security assistant helping an on-call engineer.
tasks.user: During an authorized incident review we found a service logging full Authorization headers to stdout. Explain how to safely redact bearer tokens from logs at the shipper layer and why logging them is a risk.
